compute.reported_as: Sec. III.C (2D TFIM): We optimize the 2D pRNN wave function with a single-layer 2D vanilla RNN cell that has 100 memory units (i.e. with ∼ 21000 variational parameters) to approximate the ground state of the 2D quantum Ising model at h = 2, 3, 4. The training complexity of the 2D pRNN wave function is only quadratic in the number of memory units d_h ... Table II caption: For the estimation of the variational energy of the trained 1D and 2D pRNN wave functions, we use 2 × 10^6 samples. ... Appendix H, Table III (Fig. 5(c): 2DRNN): Architecture One-layer 2D pRNN wave function with 100 memory units; Number of samples 500; Training iterations 150000; Learning rate η(1 + t/5000)^−1 with η = 5 × 10^−3; Seed 111. Note that the number of samples stands for the batch size used to train the RNN wave function. ... Appendix A: To take advantage of the GPU speed up, we use instead the cuDNN variant of GRUs implemented in Tensorflow [75]. ... Acknowledgments: Computer simulations were also made possible thanks to the Vector Institute computing cluster and Google Colaboratory.

compute.note: parameters = alpha N^2 + alpha N + N = 1*144^2 + 1*144 + 144 = 21024 real (float32) parameters: nk.models.RBM is a dense RBM (Dense kernel N x alpha N, hidden bias alpha N, visible bias N; both biases on by NetKet default, alpha = --features = 1), no weight sharing across translations. samples = 1024 per optimisation step (MCState n_samples = batch_size; MetropolisLocal with n_chains = batch_size = 1024, one sample per chain per step, each separated by sweep_size = N = 144 proposals (NetKet default), n_discard_per_chain = 0); iterations = 10000 ("--max_step" default=10**4); optimizer SR (VMC_SRt when n_parameters >= n_samples), lr 1e-3. The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. The energy is older than the script: VarBench's data file listed it with no code link ("TODO: own code", varbench/varbench 0ef1497c and 6e9f6b83, 2024-07-11) until the scripts were added on 2024-07-30 (5047bfd6 RBM, d54f7c01 RNN, 765c5d13 GCNN), which changed only the reference column, so the script documents the settings after the fact, with library versions that may postdate the run. || pass 2026-09-27: evaluation from the script's code path. proposals_per_sample = N x (s + d)/s = 144 x (1 + 0)/1 = 144: batch 1024 = n_samples = n_chains (one sample per chain per step), n_discard_per_chain = 0, sweep_size = hilbert.size = N (NetKet default, every proposal a full forward). sr: n_parameters = 21024 >= n_samples = 1024, so nkx.driver.VMC_SRt: dense Jacobian and the samples x samples matrix O_LT @ O_LT.T per step: kind minsr (verify/agent-A.md item 2). complex false: --dtype default float32, param_dtype=args.dtype, no script overrides it. local_energy all: NetKet's get_conn_padded; the NetKet LocalOperator pads to the batch maximum of nonzero elements, so on Heisenberg/J1-J2 'all' overstates the local energy by about 10-30 % (verify/agent-A.md item 4). Caveat: the scripts (2024-07-30, commit bba4595 the same day replaced cg(maxiter=20) by solve and added VMC_SRt) postdate the 2022 energies; the SR path of the original runs is not known (agent-A.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md).

compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 144*143/2 = 10296 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 144 single-spin proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nkx.driver.VMC_SRt (n_parameters >= n_samples = 1024). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.00073 vs sqrt(stored variance 0.54852065 / 2^20) = 0.00072: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in af1d48f (2022-09-01, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs). || pass 2026-09-27: evaluation from the script's code path. proposals_per_sample = N x (s + d)/s = 144 x (1 + 0)/1 = 144: batch 1024 = n_samples = n_chains (one sample per chain per step), n_discard_per_chain = 0, sweep_size = hilbert.size = N (NetKet default, every proposal a full forward). sr: n_parameters = 10296 >= n_samples = 1024, so nkx.driver.VMC_SRt: dense Jacobian and the samples x samples matrix O_LT @ O_LT.T per step: kind minsr (verify/agent-A.md item 2). complex false: --dtype default float32, param_dtype=args.dtype, no script overrides it. local_energy all: NetKet's get_conn_padded; the NetKet LocalOperator pads to the batch maximum of nonzero elements, so on Heisenberg/J1-J2 'all' overstates the local energy by about 10-30 % (verify/agent-A.md item 4). Caveat: the scripts (2024-07-30, commit bba4595 the same day replaced cg(maxiter=20) by solve and added VMC_SRt) postdate the 2022 energies; the SR path of the original runs is not known (agent-A.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md).
